title: Back in the Game
subtitle: A torch burns brightly, in the hearts of the people.

trails.title: The Aftermath
trails.description: Sending out long, dull letters is just a small part of his job.

content.text:
Subject: The "London Air Pollution Auto-detect Cleaner" Project: Progress and Future Collaboration

To the Honorable Head of the Foundation's London Division,

Allow me to extend our greetings on behalf of the London Atmospheric Clean-up Committee Office and present a thorough progress update on the "London Air Pollution Auto-detect Cleaner" initiative.

...

Though the research has faced setbacks and failed to resolve the pressing issues of the Uluru qualifiers, we greatly appreciate the open-minded approach and collaborative spirit exhibited by your department. Without your material enchantment technologies and the protocols for incantation inscription, progress would have been far more limited.

As indicated in earlier communications, we are committed to sharing the outcomes of this joint research endeavor in both mechanical engineering and arcanum studies. Although the device has not yet achieved its intended results, we will honor this commitment. As per standard collaboration practices with the Foundation, since your team provided only technical support while all material sourcing and manufacturing were conducted by us independently, the physical device will not be included in the shared materials. However, we will share its design concepts, manufacturing data, and complete test records.

...

Please accept our heartfelt gratitude for your continued cooperation. Should you require clarification or wish to discuss this matter further, please do not hesitate to reach out.

Yours sincerely,

Arthur Fog

London Atmospheric Clean-up Committee Office

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: Let's listen again to the interview she had all those years ago.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: "As the youngest Floor Ritual record holder of the century, you're just one step away from becoming the world champion. What else do you wish to achieve in your career?"

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: "My ultimate goal is to win the finals of the Uluru Games."

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: "But I'll also register for as many events as possible."

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: "I have a lot I want to achieve, but I'm patient, and I'm sure I can do it all eventually."
*clink—clunk* The sound of metal cuts through the darkness.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Now, old friend.
Willow removes her prosthetic leg, her long fingers stretching out toward the machine lubricant resting on the shelf.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: It's just you and me, isn't it?
As she gropes for the lubricant, she comes across a piece of crumpled paper.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: Careful with the scaffolding, fellas. You wouldn't want it to fall on your feet. You'll be hobblin' about for months!
Workers are busy disassembling the stage, carrying wooden posts and equipment to the door.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Here's the reimbursement application form. Just fill in the numbers and give me the receipts for the materials. I'll contact the Uluru Committee for your compensation.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: Is there really no hope, Mr. Fog? We didn't build all this just to tear it all down.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: I'm sorry.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: To be honest, we'd rather not do this, even if we are gettin' paid for it.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: We were over the moon when we got the job. I mean, just look at this place. The huge billboards and that lovely stage background.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: How could we not be? It's been yonks since we last had an event like this, and who knows when we'll have another?

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: Is there really nothin' we can do?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Excuse me. Um ...
A voice floats over from behind the ladder in the workers' arms.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: Oops! Look at me, blockin' the doorway with my ladder! Beggin' your pardon, Miss.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: That's quite alright. I'm glad to stay a little longer and talk with everyone. None of us want to leave, actually.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: How sad. But it's true. Who'd want to leave after all the trouble we've gone to?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Ms. Bartley? I must say, I didn't expect to see you here after all the qualifiers were canceled.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Hello, Mr. Fog. I'm glad to see you back on your feet.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Well, I can't wallow all day. There's a lot of cleaning up to do, and someone has to do it.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: How about you, Ms. Bartley? Will you be leaving shortly?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Yes. I suppose I'll go home and wait to hear the arrangements the committee's come up with.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Why don't you stay for a few more days?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Well, I don't think there's much point.
She looks around the almost deserted venue.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: In fact, I'm the number one seed this year, so I don't even have to participate in the qualifiers to advance to the finals.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: It's a new system they introduced to get a step closer to the standardization of human sporting events.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: I only joined because I couldn't pass up the opportunity to compete in my hometown.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: This was going to be ... the last competition of my career.
She sighs. Then, after a moment's hesitation, she speaks again.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: And I thought ... No, never mind.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: I wasn't surprised when the news came out, to be honest. We were just fooling ourselves before, and now it's time to face the fact that—

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: Sorry to interrupt you, but ain't it too early to be gettin' this dark, Mr. Fog?
The three of them look up at the sky as the world is plunged into darkness.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Crikey. What time is it, mate?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: I don't have to look at my watch to know it isn't night yet.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Then what's going on?
The thick black-and-yellow smog surges upward, like a massive arm poised to sweep them away.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Whoa! What the bloody hell is happening?!

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Are you alright?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: All good, thanks. What the blazes was that?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: It looked just like the black fog that attacked the hospital.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Only smaller. And it was a different shape.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Let's move to your office, Mr. Fog. There's something we need to talk about.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I believe all these problems we're having—the smog, the tuberculosis, the failure of your machine—have something to do with the black fog.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: But first, we need to get everyone out of the stadium in case it attacks again.
Upon entering the office, Brimley heads straight to the purifier and gives its glass top a curious tap.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Leave it be. It's no use worrying about it now.
Mr. Fog glances at his once-revered purification machine, now sitting inert in the corner.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: You pushed it too hard, mate.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Don't be too hard on yourself, Mr. Fog. The fact that you made something that worked at all in just a matter of weeks is an achievement in itself.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Haha, I appreciate it, Ms. Tooth Fairy. I know it doesn't make any sense to keep it around after it failed so spectacularly, but I just ... ugh!
He tries to raise it off the ground to shift it, but doesn't succeed.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: I can't bear to break it down. At least not for now. I enchanted it with my arcane skill, so we're linked together. It used to breathe as I did, and now I cough and splutter just like it does. *cough*

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: You should go to the hospital as soon as possible.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: See? How many times have I told you that, and you never listened?! Even the doctor's saying so!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Anyway, what was it that you wanted to talk about, Ms. Tooth Fairy?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: The experiments I've been doing these days. Here's a sample of the black fog. I collected it from the alley after it attacked me.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: As for the tuberculosis, I analyzed the black fog's composition and found some components very similar to those in the patients' saliva. I've concluded that this fog critter is the root cause of the disease.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: This critter is fog-soluble, can change its form, and is indestructible. It feeds on smog, and, most interestingly, sensitive emotions, which it seems to absorb to nourish itself.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: In conclusion, the answer to our problems lies in capturing and containing these critters.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Also, in one of my experiments, I cultured two samples under the same conditions and put one of them in the sun, like this.
Tooth Fairy delicately places the bottle containing the black critter on the windowsill.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: See? Even in today's dim sunlight, it shrinks very quickly.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Just wait a moment, and you'll see ...

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Its true being.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Sunlight is their weakness. That's why you never see them in areas with clear skies.
She pauses, as if to add gravity to her point.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: As you can see, London provides the perfect conditions for it to survive and multiply: heavy smog and the anxiety and depression caused by the cancelation of the qualifiers.
A thoughtful silence falls in the office.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: I do believe you're right, but it won't be easy to capture these things.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: No, definitely not.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I'm still trying to figure that one out. We may be able to lure them into a trap, but we need to make a specific plan so that the process is controllable and the results predictable.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: A specific plan? The only plan I can think of is to pray to God!

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Some people may seek answers from the divine, but whether that works or not is another matter.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oi!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Helloooo!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Is that Flutterpage's voice?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Sure is. Over there, mate. Outside the window!
There's a tap at the window.
Outside, Flutterpage drifts in the air, a white bedsheet clutched in her hands. Below her, a crowd of all ages makes their way along Cross Street, all heading for the sports stadium.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Tooth Fairy, Mr. Fog, Mr. Brimley! Would you like to join us?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: The residents of Cross Street have got together to petition for the reopenin' of the qualifiers!
Flutterpage uses one hand to steady the bedsheet and the other to point excitedly at the crowd congregating below.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Oi, folks! How 'bout this iron? It's a family heirloom, but it'll be perfect for the Floating Shot Fling!

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: And I'll be the stopwatch! I'm an excellent timekeeper. I can keep time down to the millisecond!

items.speaker: Neighbor II
items.text: We also need a fair judge, right? Then I'll put myself forward! Everyone on Cross Street knows I'm an excellent mediator!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Everyone's brought things from their homes! Ladders, hangin' rods, clotheslines, anythin' that might be useful. We're goin' to rebuild the stadium together!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: So? Will you join us?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: What? Are you serious?!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Strewth! I don't know what to say. This is unbelievable!
The crowd pushes on to the stadium, a few individuals joining the throng as they pass by their homes.
There is a resolute happiness in the air, as though no force could diminish their fervent hope.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Since the qualifiers have been canceled, we'll just have to hold our own Games.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Tooth Fairy, I've found the right way to look at the fish tank.
